questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: Moves in the opening of a procedure
questions.learningObjective: Identify a purpose statement in the opening

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: The sentence states the aim, which is the goal. A marginal reminder adds: does it say why. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: The rule to carry into this item is “Identify a purpose statement in the opening / Does it say why? / Moves in the opening of a procedure”. Which option applies it?

options.text: It defines the scope of the procedure.
It states the goal of the procedure.
It names the intended audience.
It sets a safety limit.
options.misconception: treats a target as a hazard control

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: the sentence states the aim, which is the goal. On that basis "It states the goal of the procedure" is the supported choice. Option A ("It defines the scope of the procedure") fails because it confuses goal with scope; Option C ("It names the intended audience") fails because it mistakes goal for audience; Option D ("It sets a safety limit") fails because it treats a target as a hazard control.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: The check a step needs before it is done
questions.learningObjective: Identify a missing pre-check

stimulus.body: Fit the new filter. Secure the housing. Start the engine and listen for abnormal noise. If normal, record the service and return the unit. before starting, the filter and housing must be confirmed. A marginal reminder adds: what must be true before power. Four statements are offered, and only one follows from the note.

questions.stem: Apply “Identify a missing pre-check / What must be true before power? / The check a step needs before it is done” to the four options. Which one is supported?

options.text: Verify the mechanic's name.
Check the engine's colour.
Confirm the filter is seated and housing secured.
Measure the garage temperature.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: before starting, the filter and housing must be confirmed. On that basis "Confirm the filter is seated and housing secured" is the supported choice. Option A ("Verify the mechanic's name") fails because it confuses identity with readiness; Option B ("Check the engine's colour") fails because it focuses on appearance; Option D ("Measure the garage temperature") fails because it adds an unrelated check.
questions.hint: What must be true before power?

questions.topic: A part named two different ways
questions.learningObjective: Spot a part renamed mid-procedure

questions.stem: The passage is read with “Spot a part renamed mid-procedure / Could two names mean two parts? / A part named two different ways” as the test. Which option meets it?

options.text: The seal is now a tool.
The seal becomes optional.
The seal must be replaced between steps.
options.misconception: treats a name change as a part change

options.text: A reader may fetch the wrong seal.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: two names for one seal suggest two distinct items, risking the wrong part. On that basis "A reader may fetch the wrong seal" is the supported choice. Option A ("The seal is now a tool") fails because it confuses label with category; Option B ("The seal becomes optional") fails because it treats renaming as optionality; Option C ("The seal must be replaced between steps") fails because it treats a name change as a part change.
questions.hint: Could two names mean two parts?

questions.topic: A quantity that cannot be measured as written
questions.learningObjective: Identify a subjective quantity

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: The phrase gives no measurable endpoint. A marginal reminder adds: how clean is thorough. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: The excerpt is probed with “Identify a subjective quantity / How clean is thorough? / A quantity that cannot be measured as written”. Which choice is defensible?

answer.exemplar: 'Thoroughly' names no method, duration, or cleanliness standard, so operators stop at different points and the result cannot be verified against a specification.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the phrase gives no measurable endpoint. On that basis "Thoroughly' names no method, duration, or cleanliness standard, so operators stop at different…" is the supported choice.

options.text: In the tools list.
After the step, as a note.

questions.stem: The rule to carry into this item is “Recognise a section-wide limit / A banner covers its section. / A limit stated once for many steps”. Which option applies it?

options.text: The revision history.
Only the first step.
The tools list.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: An irreversible step left unmarked
questions.learningObjective: Flag an irreversible action without warning

stimulus.body: Step 22: Cut the retaining strap with a knife. Step 23: Remove the cover. Step 24: Inspect the internals. The brief contains no caution symbols or notes.

questions.stem: Step 22: Cut the retaining strap with a knife. Step 23: Remove the cover. Step 24: Inspect the internals. The brief contains no caution symbols or notes. In an engineer's design brief, which step is destructive and unmarked?

options.text: Step 23, because removing a cover cannot be undone.
Step 22, because cutting the strap is permanent.
Step 24, because inspection alters internals.
None, because the brief is concise.
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "None, because the brief is concise" for the governing rule

questions.explanation: Cutting the retaining strap is irreversible. Removing a cover and inspecting are reversible or observational, and conciseness is not a safety signal.
